design:
## Design tests

Each weak visual was refined on the isolation bench first (`vision/isolation_v014.md`): the template forced alone into a picture, cut out with nothing else around it and read blind by a fresh reader, four rounds and 52 images in all, two of them side-by-side readings of competing drawings in the same scenes. The bench caught several first attempts: a lower stalking crouch read as "running or creeping toward the bird"; the stuck girl reaching out to the man read as "pointing or waving"; two arcs either side of a hand by a child's head read as "holding a phone to her ear"; a rack hoop behind the square-wheeled bicycle turned its wheels into "square wheel-holder frames that belong to the rack"; a twig across the stuck ball made it a blue cap; the flying kite, leaning toward its flyer, kept "the string and the bow tail both come off the kite's bottom point".

The refined visuals were then read blind in whole test scenes among other events (`vision/design_tests_v014.md`, three rounds, eleven pictures). They added six placement rules: short wave arcs (two long ones closed into "a faint thin circle or ring" round the hand); no dog at the stalking cat's depth of the picture (a dog walking toward it "could lunge"); the blown cap never the colour of a cap someone else wears; nobody downwind of the cap or in the gust's path (a cap blowing toward a man sweeping "could be the man's"); an empty swing swung by the gust; and the fence-top stalking cat clear of the clothesline. In the last round the stalking cat read as "crouched low and creeping toward a blue bird ... about to pounce", the girl on the seesaw as "stuck up there because the reader is not pushing off", and the gust as "a strong breeze blowing from right to left ... laundry ... flapping sideways in the wind".

Inspecting every built picture added one more rule: no kite or balloon string between a stalking cat and its bird (one layout ran a kite string down between them on the fence top). The tier-3 garden picture it changed was rebuilt.
intro: Two of the three templates that failed in v0.13 pass the eleventh screen with full marks in every picture: the stalking cat, now with the ground to itself ("crouched low, creeping up behind the bird ... as if about to pounce"), and the heavy man on the seesaw, with the girl's legs hanging and her face turned to us ("his weight is keeping the girl up ... he doesn't seem to notice her, so she's stuck"). The set scored 0.995 over all items, the best of the eleven screens, with no item misread and 1.3 unintended oddities per picture (2.1 in v0.13); 63 of 64 templates pass the gate. The one failure is the wave, on a single misread in a probe: an older man waving toward a woman whose hose had stopped read as "scratching his head ... looking puzzled".
screen: Across all 60 pictures only 4 of 703 scored items fell short of full marks (8 of 717 in v0.13): three half points on inferences in the set, two walkers heading for a bucket set a little to one side of their path ("he may walk into it, or he may just pass it") and a bird at a sandwich never said to be stealing it, and one misread in a probe, the wave. Unintended oddities in the set fell from 44 to 28. None of the v0.13 oddities came back as reported then: nobody seemed to stand on an empty seesaw, no bicycle stood "by itself", no ball was "drawn on top of the tree", no kite string met the tail, no black cat slept unreadably, no dropped scoop was outsized and no lead ran round a dog's middle. What remains is mostly drawing depth (a low bush and the bird table's pole half hidden by the garden fence), wind that still leaves hair unmoved, and situations rather than drawing (a goat in a back garden, a hose across a path).
redrawn: The stalking cat and the seesaw read with full marks in all three of their pictures. The visuals refined for the v0.13 oddities kept full marks: the ball "stuck on a branch" in all five pictures, the square wheels in all three, the windy hat in all three ("It is windy ... just had his orange cap blown off"), the dropped ice cream in all six and the sleeping cats and dogs "curled up asleep" in all six. The wave lost its point in one of three pictures, all three adults; no child waved in the screened pictures.
gate: Every template was screened in at least three pictures (54 in three, 6 in four, 2 in five, 2 in six). The wave fails on one misread in one picture: it carries one item per picture, so a single reading decides it. The v0.15 fix is to wave only toward someone free of any mishap, with a probe that shows a waving child.
